nodes.label: Voyage as direct competitor
nodes.rationale: Voyage directly competes on unscripted AI-DM with world memory and multiplayer. If it reaches maturity in 2H 2026, it will own the space unless this plan's differentiators (dark-fantasy IP, permadeath, cross-playthrough NPC memory) prove defensible.

nodes.label: Cross-playthrough NPC memory + recall surfacing
nodes.rationale: No shipped platform found with persistent NPCs that resurface across completed, separate playthroughs. This plan's post-v1 recall node (named returning face) + chronicle-ledger are genuinely novel differentiators.

nodes.label: Permadeath + Torpor as core stakes
nodes.rationale: Permadeath is designed as intentional game mechanic, not accident of content policy. Combined with Torpor soft-buffer and character permanence, this stakes-based design is intentional vs accident.

nodes.label: DOM+CSS-first frontend architecture
nodes.rationale: For text+card game, DOM+CSS is optimal. Text and card UI are DOM's sweet spot; eliminates physics, collision, tilemap code bloat unused by this game. No engine bloat for systems never used.

nodes.label: Tension with Foundational Decision #19-21 (Phaser/PixiJS)
nodes.rationale: Research finding flags Phaser as potentially overkill. For 90% text+cards, 10% sprite tweens, DOM+CSS is lighter and defensible. Not an override, but candidate amendment pending future review.

nodes.label: LangGraph.js current orchestration
nodes.rationale: LangGraph.js used for 4-node linear pipeline (resolve → validate → narrate → art). Slightly over-engineered for this linear scope, but overhead is negligible and code clarity is good. Switching gains no functionality.
